question: True or false: a national film body has refused to fund films whose villains are marked out by facial scars?
answer: True. In 2018 the British Film Institute said it would no longer fund films that signal villainy through scars or facial difference, backing the charity Changing Faces' campaign I Am Not Your Villain. Decades of scarred villains had taught audiences to read a marked face as a warning, a lesson real people carry daily.
move: Shortcuts that tell an audience who is bad also teach them whom to fear.
ask: Whose face or look do I read as a warning, and where did I learn that?
trap: False, because funders are assumed to stay out of creative choices.
